note:
DEAR Dr. Hoffmann,

I am referring my patient, Margot Krause, 66 years old, to your care for further evaluation of symptomatic anemia.

HISTORY
The patient reports progressive fatigue, dizziness, and exertional dyspnea for three months. She noticed pallor and brittle nails. She denies melena, hematochezia, or hematuria. She recently traveled to Vienna two weeks ago but denies dietary indiscretion or illness.

EXAMINATION
Vital signs: BP 110/70, HR 92, Temp 36.8.
General: Pallor noted.
Cardiovascular: Systolic murmur heard at the 3 o'clock position, grade 2/6.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no hepatosplenomegaly.

LABS
CBC ordered. Iron studies, ferritin, B12, and folate levels pending.

PLAN
1. Referral for upper and lower endoscopy to rule out occult GI bleeding.
2. Iron supplementation started.
3. Follow-up blood work in one week.

Please contact my office at 089 123 456 78 with your findings.

Sincerely,
Dr. Weber
Medizinische Praxis am Starnberger See
Patient Insurance: Techniker Krankenkasse, TK 123 456 789 01
dialogue:
[doctor] Good morning, Mrs. Krause. I am Dr. Weber. I am here for your home visit today.
[patient] Oh, good morning, Doctor. Thank you for coming. Um, please, come in.
[doctor] Thank you. The light in here is quite nice. How have you been feeling since we last spoke?
[patient] Honestly? Not great. I’ve been feeling really tired. Just... drained. Like I can’t shake it.
[doctor] How long has this fatigue been going on?
[patient] Uh, for about three months. It started slowly, but now it’s pretty bad.
[doctor] I see. Do you have any other symptoms? Dizziness, shortness of breath?
[patient] Yes, yes. Dizziness when I stand up too fast. And my heart feels like it’s beating fast, even when I’m just sitting here.
[doctor] Have you noticed any changes in your skin or nails?
[patient] Oh, my skin looks very pale, I think. My daughter said I look "ghostly" yesterday. And my nails are breaking easily.
[doctor] That can happen with low blood count. Do you have any pain in your chest or abdomen?
[patient] No chest pain, thank goodness. But sometimes I feel a bit bloated.
[doctor] Have you had any gastrointestinal bleeding? Dark stools or blood in your urine?
[patient] I don’t think so. My stools are normal. I’m not on any blood thinners, just some vitamins.
[doctor] Good. Let’s take a look at your heart and lungs. Can you lie down on the sofa for a moment?
[patient] Sure. Oh, my back is a bit stiff from lying in bed.
[doctor] Take your time. I’ll use the stethoscope.
[patient] It’s cold!
[doctor] Sorry. Let me warm it up. I’m listening to your heart now.
[patient] Is there something wrong?
[doctor] I hear a systolic murmur. It’s loudest at the 3 o'clock position. It’s likely a flow murmur due to the anemia, but we need to confirm.
[patient] Anemia? Like my mother had?
[doctor] Yes, that’s a possibility. We need blood tests to check your hemoglobin levels. I will order a complete blood count and iron studies.
[patient] Will I need a transfusion?
[doctor] Not immediately, unless your levels are very low. But we need to find out why this is happening. Have you had any recent illnesses?
[patient] I went to Vienna two weeks ago. I was fine there, but maybe the jet lag... well, it’s not jet lag, it’s within Europe, but the time difference...
[doctor] Vienna is only one hour ahead. Did you eat anything unusual there?
[patient] Oh, we had a lot of sausage. And wine. But nothing strange.
[doctor] I see. Do you have any history of stomach ulcers or colon problems?
[patient] No, I had a colonoscopy five years ago, it was clear.
[doctor] That’s good. I will refer you to a gastroenterologist to rule out any hidden bleeding. Do you have your insurance card with you?
[patient] Yes, here. I am with Techniker Krankenkasse.
[doctor] Thank you. What is your insurance number?
[patient] It’s TK 123 456 789 01.
[doctor] Noted. I will send the referral letter to <ORGANization>Gastro-Praxis am Rathaus in Munich.
[patient] Oh, that’s convenient. It’s close to where I live.
[doctor] Yes. In the meantime, please start taking an iron supplement. I will prescribe it for you.
[patient] Iron makes my stomach upset, though.
[doctor] Take it with food, but avoid taking it with tea or coffee, as they block absorption.
[patient] Understood. Do I need to change my diet?
[doctor] Eat more iron-rich foods like red meat, spinach, and lentils. But remember, the most important thing is to find the cause of the blood loss or deficiency.
[patient] I hope it’s just a vitamin deficiency. I’m scared it’s something worse.
[doctor] It’s too early to know. But many causes are treatable. Let’s wait for the blood results. I will call you in three days.
[patient] Thank you, Doctor. I feel a bit better knowing someone is checking.
[doctor] You are welcome. I will leave the prescription here. If you feel faint or have chest pain, please call 112 immediately.
[patient] Okay. I will rest now.
[doctor] Get some rest. I’ll see you soon.
